title: WB2A natural burner/A1 runtime correlation and volatile control-surface evidence

0xA305.note: Observed as a modulation-related output state, not as an independent burner-demand flag.

0x555A.description: Effective boiler target considering boiler max temperature, boiler protection and frost protection; Vitosoft explicitly states startup optimization is not included.

operating_mode_transition.interpretation: A1/HKP1 and the integrated-pump relay state become active well before burner startup.

coding_plug_candidates.caution: The measured approximately 240 s restart interval is numerically consistent, but this capture alone does not isolate GWG65 from other 240 s mechanisms.
Also numerically 240 s. Do not attribute the observed restart interval uniquely to GWG65 or GWG73 without a stronger discriminator.

coding_plug_candidates.observation: Kesselsoll_eff reproducibly drops 38 -> 18 C immediately before both startup sequences, an exact 20 K difference.
coding_plug_candidates.caution: Strong numerical/temporal correlation only. Kesselsoll_eff's source description says startup optimization itself is not included; the precise firmware relation to GWG72 is not yet proven.

established: Across two natural direct-A1 burner starts, A1 pump speed remained exactly 32% before startup, during the pre-flame GFA sequence, throughout flame and through flame-off.
No burner-dependent A1 speed boost was visible in the active VDensHO1 configuration.
A152 HKP1 and internal-pump relay bits are active before burner startup and remain unchanged through the flame cycle.
A152 nvoRelayState_Brenner remained 0 even while independent flame channels were 1, so that LON relay bit is not the local GFA burner request/output path on this installation.
A305 follows the modulation state and is not an independent pre-flame burner-demand flag.
0x0A3A stayed 0 and therefore does not reveal a hidden A1 speed result on this topology.
not_established: Absence of an observed A1 boost does not prove the firmware contains no dormant/alternate burner-dependent pump algorithm.
No volatile pump-control write surface has yet been exercised.
No causal assignment of the approximately 240 s interval to GWG65 versus GWG73 is made.
No causal assignment of the 20 K Kesselsoll_eff offset to GWG72 is made yet.

noteworthy: 0xA380 nviProdCmd_CFDM value/state: volatile production-output command, Virtual_READ/Virtual_WRITE
No exact VDensHO1 nvi pump-speed command exists in the recovered service groups.
exact_vdensho1_nvi_trace.interpretation: The CFDM surface is a heat-production-demand interface, not a source-backed A1 pump-speed interface. It is not a candidate for direct pump-speed control.

next_boundary: Vitosoft-exposed service, LON nvi and KBus write surfaces do not reveal a volatile direct-A1 pump-speed override for VDensHO1.
Do not repurpose CFDM production commands or relay-test functions as a pump-speed solution.
Continue at controller-firmware/MCU level once local PCB/MCU identity is available.
Use the physical coding-plug EEPROM read as the next independent evidence path when available.

result: A1 runtime surfaces 0x7663 and 0x0A3A are read-only (FCWrite undefined).
Internal-pump runtime/result surfaces 0x7660 and 0x0A3C are read-only.
A1 E6/E7/E8/E9 are Virtual_WRITE coding surfaces, not separate runtime speed commands.
K30/K31/K32/K34 and 6C are also Virtual_WRITE coding/configuration surfaces.
0x7500 RelaistestGWG200x is a diagnostic relay-test surface; it is not a source-backed A1 speed-control algorithm.
No exact VDensHO1 pump-related event exposes a dedicated volatile A1 speed-command surface.

global_kbus_pump_write_scan.conclusion: No VDensHO1/HO1 KBus write event with pump/speed semantics exists in the recovered All-Devices catalog.
